concept.name: Market structure break
concept.definition: In price-structure analysis, a break of the swing sequence defining the current trend: in an uptrend, a close below the most recent higher low (or, in continuation terms, a close above the prior swing high that extends the structure). SMC/ICT usage distinguishes a trend-continuing break of structure from a counter-trend structure shift; the terminology is a discretionary convention without a single canonical authority.
concept.intuition: The market's staircase pattern breaks a step — the rhythm of higher floors or lower ceilings is violated, so the structure may be changing.
concept.mechanics: Map swing highs and lows; a trend-continuing BOS prints when price exceeds the last swing high in an uptrend (or undercuts the last swing low in a downtrend), while a structure break against the trend prints when the last higher low (or lower high) is taken out. Confirmation conventions vary: some require a close beyond the swing, others a wick.
concept.failure_modes: Marginal wick-throughs of a swing look like structure breaks but resolve as stop runs; and without a fixed swing-definition rule, two analysts mark different structures on the same chart.
concept.misconceptions: That a single broken swing proves trend reversal; a wick through a level that closes back inside is a sweep, not a break — acceptance beyond the level is the distinguishing test.
concept.example: An uptrend with higher lows at 50, 52, 54 breaks down when price closes below 54: the structure break flips bias from buying dips to selling rallies.
